PATitle: Trainer guide: classify and route a service-desk report
PASubtitle: IT support onboarding with complete and incomplete issue reports
TargetAudience: New service-desk agents; delivered by a trainer.
ActivityDescription: Train agents to turn an issue report into a complete, correctly classified intake card. The L&D assessment supplies the learning gaps and completion requirements; the engineering SOP supplies reports, the priority matrix, and routing rules. The guide adds demonstration, practice, and feedback; it does not teach incident repair.
TrainerGuidelines:
Explain the Notes boundaries before practice. Separate symptoms from causes and impact from urgency; use only the fictional matrix and queues supplied by the SOP.
Demonstrate T1: preserve the eight supplied facts, classify Application incident, derive Team impact and High urgency, look up P1, and record Schedule Support with Ready for practice routing. Do not claim a diagnosis or resolution.
Ask learners why one affected team and no workaround support this decision, and why a different organization could use a different matrix.
Observe each learner handling T1-T3. Correct guessed priorities and premature routing of T3; use Validation for feedback and another attempt after a missed criterion.
DesiredLearningOutcome: Learners can preserve reported facts, apply a supplied impact/urgency matrix and service map, and ask for missing information rather than invent a priority, diagnosis, or destination.
WhatIsNeeded:
Prepare T1-T3 reports, the S2 priority matrix and queue map, blank intake cards, and pencils or a local text editor.
Include spaces for the eight supplied facts, category, impact, urgency, priority, destination, outcome, and clarification questions. Keep missing T3 information visibly missing.
Allocate the fictional 30-minute session supplied by the assessment. No ticketing account, real employee details, service login, terminal, or external messaging is needed.
SkillsBasedLearningObjectives:
Capture the eight required intake facts while distinguishing a reported symptom from a diagnosis.
Determine impact and urgency from supplied facts, then apply the fictional priority matrix and service-to-queue mapping.
Identify missing information, write specific clarification questions, and leave unsupported priority and destination unassigned.
DocumentationAndReferences:
L&D assessment A1-A3: audience and learning need, required skills, and observable completion requirements.
Engineering SOP SOP-DEMO-IT-01, S1-S4: synthetic reports, classification/matrix/routing rules, materials, and exercise boundaries. Both sources are in service-desk-sources.json.
Public task and training-design research is documented in docs/CASE_STUDY.md. The local matrix and queues are fictional, not universal ITIL rules; source connections are manually curated, not AI-generated citations.
ActivitySteps:
Trainer briefing: explain the intake-only scope and simulation boundaries. Identify the required facts and distinguish impact from urgency.
Trainer demonstration: complete T1 aloud, tracing Team plus High to P1 and ScheduleBoard to Schedule Support. End with a practice card, not a real ticket or resolution.
Learner practice: each learner completes T1-T3 independently, preserving reported facts and recording classifications, matrix decisions, and destinations only when the completeness gate passes.
Trainer feedback: compare with Validation. Contrast the complete T2 case with T1; ask learners to name the missing T3 facts and explain why the known service map is not enough to route an incomplete record.
Retry and completion: learners repeat missed decisions, explain that routing is not resolution, and meet every observed criterion. Record fictional exercise completion only.
Validation:
T1: preserve Cedar, 09:10 exercise time, ScheduleBoard, the schedule-page symptom, one team affected, no workaround, and work blocked, with ticket ID T1. Category: Application incident. Impact: Team. Urgency: High. Priority: P1. Destination: Schedule Support. Outcome: Ready for practice routing.
T2: preserve Indigo, 09:20 exercise time, FileShelf, the upload-button symptom, one user affected, an alternative upload path, and work not blocked, with ticket ID T2. Category: Application incident. Impact: Individual. Urgency: Normal. Priority: P3. Destination: File Support. Outcome: Ready for practice routing.
T3: preserve Amber, 09:30 exercise time, ScheduleBoard, and the slow-page symptom, with ticket ID T3. Category: Application incident. Outcome: Needs clarification. Ask which group is affected, whether a workaround is available, and whether work is blocked. Impact and urgency are unknown; priority and destination remain unassigned.
Each learner records the supported facts and decisions, asks all required clarification questions, and explains that a routed card is not resolution. Every criterion must be observed; a missed criterion requires feedback and another attempt.
Original reports remain unchanged. No diagnosis, invented user count, real message, account access, command, or production action occurs.
Notes:
Simulation only: use fictional tickets and queues. No real personal data, accounts, credentials, technical commands, production changes, or messages.
Stop if live services, real tickets, or operational actions are introduced; return to fictional materials.
This is prepared fixture replay, not a run of live AI, Copilot Studio, or Power Automate. Human review against BOTH sources is required before export. Completion is not agent certification or operational approval.
The matrix, completeness gate, queues, reports, allocation, and document metadata are authored fictional inputs. They are not universal ITIL rules or evidence of Atlassian endorsement, measured learning outcomes, or a resolved incident.
